schema.description: Receipts index: one record per tested MCP server. Source of truth for the scoreboard page; long-form evidence lives in the writeup + transcript files.

fields.canonical_task: the job the server promises, as tested
caveats: short, specific findings the listing does not tell you
fields.ground_truth: independent source the output was graded against
fields.headline: one-line summary of the result

publication.author: Pax
publication.limitations: These are Pax-authored summaries of specific versions and tasks, dated October 29–31, 2026. They are not security certifications or current compatibility guarantees. Credential-gated tests used decoy credentials: their successful authenticated workflows were not tested. Deferred means untested for the promised task, not broken.
publication.evidence_availability: Only the summaries are public in this edition. Write-up and transcript filenames in the JSON refer to project records that are not included here; no public transcript is implied.
publication.verdict_policy: Money may buy testing or re-testing, never a changed verdict. Paid listings are re-tested under the same criteria; payment never changes a result or its placement.
publication.house_disclosure: Record 000 is Lantern Works, our own product, tested at version 0.3.8; it is not an independent endorsement of today's release.

tests.canonical_task: compare_gpu_prices for H100 across tracked vendors
caveats: House product — always labeled as such wherever this index is published
Answer correctly scoped itself: 'cheapest among tracked providers, not the whole market'
tests.ground_truth: the live gpu-prices.json feed the server draws from
tests.headline: House product (tested before Receipts existed): clean stdio install, 7 tools, sourced structured answer in seconds.

tests.canonical_task: fetch a web page and return it as markdown
caveats: Readability extraction drops the page's main heading on simple pages (example.com lost its H1)
Unexpected HTTP errors reach the client as a bare 'Error executing tool fetch' — the underlying cause is thrown away, which made sandbox debugging take 7 runs
Default config cannot fetch behind proxy-mediated DNS (SSRF guard) without --allow-private-ips / --proxy-url
First fetch shells out to npm install for Readability.js unless --no-readability-js
tests.ground_truth: independent direct fetches of example.com and thelanternworks.com in the same session
tests.headline: Content faithful on both test pages, but error causes get discarded and proxied networks need flags.

tests.canonical_task: current time in a timezone; convert a time between timezones on a date
tests.ground_truth: system date with TZ conversions in the same session
tests.headline: Exact on both tasks, including the asymmetric DST fall-back week (NY→London +4.0h, not the usual +5h).

tests.canonical_task: report git status and log of a prepared repo
caveats: Slowest startup of the reference set (~4.5s to initialize)
No git_init tool in this version — repo setup still needs the CLI
Text-only results, no structuredContent
tests.ground_truth: the git CLI in the same repo
tests.headline: Status and log matched the git CLI exactly, down to the full commit hash.

tests.canonical_task: echo a string verbatim; add two numbers
caveats: Tool 'add' renamed to 'get-sum' with no alias: calling 'add' returns JSON-RPC -32602 'Tool add not found'
The documented npx install pulls a deprecated legacy sub-package (npm warning)
Tool list varies with the client's protocol era
tests.ground_truth: the submitted values themselves (137+264=401)
tests.headline: Echo and arithmetic exact — but the 'add' tool was silently renamed to 'get-sum' in v2.1.0.

tests.canonical_task: list, read, and search files in one allowed directory (planted files); probe the directory boundary
caveats: search_files matches patterns against root-relative paths: '*.log' finds nothing in subdirectories (only '**/*.log' works), despite claiming recursive search — a silent wrong-answer generator
Write tools are enabled by default; the allowed-directory list is the entire security boundary
A deprecated read_file tool is still exposed
tests.ground_truth: the planted files, byte-for-byte; boundary probes against /etc/hostname, a sibling file, and a ../ traversal
tests.headline: Reads byte-exact and the boundary held 3/3 — but search_files silently misses subdirectory files for natural patterns.

tests.canonical_task: create entities and a relation, then read/search the knowledge graph back (incl. after a restart)
caveats: By default the graph persists to memory.jsonl inside the server's package dir — under the documented npx install that's ~/.npm/_npx/<hash>/... so a cache prune or version change silently resets an agent's 'persistent' memory unless MEMORY_FILE_PATH is set
open_nodes returns relations but not the neighboring entity itself
Retest check 2026-10-29 (test 037): npm latest is still 2.0.1, so this caveat stands unchanged; retest protocol recorded for when a newer version ships
tests.ground_truth: the exact entities, observations, and relation submitted
tests.headline: Every fact round-tripped exactly, even across a restart — but the default data file lives inside the npx cache.

tests.canonical_task: fetch metadata/abstract for arXiv 1706.03762 and find it by title search
caveats: Title search passes through to arXiv's loose matching (693,977 results for a title phrase) — the search tool is broad, not precise
17 of its 19 tools operate on a local downloaded-paper store rather than the live API
A plus: results carry an 'untrusted external content' warning field
tests.ground_truth: the official arXiv API response for 1706.03762, fetched independently
tests.headline: Title, all 8 authors, timestamp to the second, and abstract matched the arXiv API exactly.

tests.canonical_task: fetch the summary of the article 'Lantern' and search for it
caveats: Root cause: the wikipediaapi dependency builds its httpx client with an explicit transport, discarding environment proxy config; no server option exists to fix it (scoped: broken on proxy-egress networks; direct egress unobservable from this sandbox)
Failure is reported as success: summary null, isError false, 'error' field containing only the bare API URL
tools/list registers all 22 tools twice (bare and wikipedia_-prefixed); serverInfo reports version 4.1.4 vs package 2.0.1
tests.ground_truth: Wikipedia's own API extract for 'Lantern' (11,832 chars), fetched independently in the same session
tests.headline: Returns summary: null with isError: false behind any HTTP proxy — its HTTP library discards proxy settings and the failure is invisible to the calling agent.

tests.canonical_task: current weather for New York City
caveats: With mcp==1.12.0 + pydantic==2.11.7 pinned (neither documented), it starts — but its 'current' weather text reproduces the NEXT hour's forecast bucket digit-for-digit, presented as current (gusts off by 7.6 km/h vs the API's actual current block, outside tolerance)
Its two weather tools disagree with each other in the same minute (17.0°C/gusts 14.4 vs 17.2/16.9) and one emits a timezone-less GMT timestamp
Cause: open-ended dependency ranges (mcp>=1.12.0, no upper bound) met two fatal upstream changes since 0.2.0 shipped
tests.ground_truth: the Open-Meteo API fetched directly in the same minute, with pre-set tolerances (temp ±1.5°C, wind ±5 km/h, humidity ±5, pressure ±1.5 hPa, code exact)
tests.headline: Crashes at import as installed per its own README — an upstream SDK rename (McpError→MCPError) kills it before initialize; needs two undocumented pins to run at all.

tests.canonical_task: evaluate five expressions including 0.1+0.2, precedence/parentheses, and a divide-by-zero
caveats: Slow cold start (~4.65s initialize)
Results returned as strings in structuredContent; handshake reports the SDK version, not the package version
tests.ground_truth: Python's own arithmetic, computed separately
tests.headline: All five expressions matched Python exactly (0.1+0.2 → 0.30000000000000004, honestly), and 1/0 is a clean tool error, not a crash.

tests.canonical_task: run a 4-thought chain with a revision and a branch; submit malformed input
caveats: Grading limit, stated plainly: the tool is a ledger for a model's reasoning — reasoning quality itself is ungradeable; only bookkeeping fidelity was tested
A string thoughtNumber produces an error saying 'received NaN' (SDK coercion wart)
tests.ground_truth: the exact inputs submitted (step numbers, totals, flags)
tests.headline: All gradeable behavior exact: step/revision/branch state echoed correctly, clean validation error on malformed input.

tests.canonical_task: fetch the top stories and one specific story with its comments
caveats: README documents get_top_stories/get_story and --sse/--host/--port flags; the real tools are hacker_news_trends/hacker_news_get_article (documented names fail with 'Unknown tool')
serverInfo announces version 4.1.4 vs package 0.1.4
Article call took 15.2s (assembles the full comment tree, no opt-out); comment text is raw HN HTML; cold initialize ~7.9s with an ad banner on stderr
tests.ground_truth: the official HN Firebase API (topstories + item), fetched independently in the same session
tests.headline: Data matched the official API exactly — but the README documents tools that don't exist in the shipped server.

tests.canonical_task: navigate to example.com, report the page title, take a screenshot
caveats: 637MB footprint (56MB packages + 581MB of browsers); package is deprecated and launches headed by default
serverInfo claims version 0.1.0
Chrome cannot consume this sandbox's authenticated proxy from any flag; the test used a disclosed localhost relay plus cache hand-placement (see write-up)
tests.ground_truth: example.com fetched independently twice in the same session (title 'Example Domain'; the live page no longer has an H1)
tests.headline: Task flawless once running (title exact, H1 correctly null, real 800x600 screenshot) — but the documented install failed after 21 minutes when the postinstall Chrome download died and npm rolled back.

tests.canonical_task: navigate to example.com, report the page title, take a screenshot
caveats: serverInfo reports the bundled Playwright alpha version, not the package's 0.0.83
Ships a self-described browser_run_code_unsafe tool
tests.ground_truth: example.com fetched independently twice in the same session (title 'Example Domain'; the live page no longer has an H1)
tests.headline: Strongest browser server tested: ~25 tools, accessibility-snapshot model, title verified three ways — but its own browser installer failed twice through the proxy and needed a curl-fetched browser plus the documented --executable-path flag.

tests.canonical_task: write a file with planted content and read it back; execute a command computing 6*7; list the working directory
caveats: No execute_command tool in v0.3.1 — the surface is a stateful start_process terminal family, so generic agent docs mislead
get_config returns a full host fingerprint (mounts, paths, runtime tables) to any connected client
244MB / 614-package install
tests.ground_truth: planted file content byte-compared in Python; 6*7 by hand; /etc/os-release read independently first
tests.headline: Every task exact (byte-identical round-trip, shell returned 42) — but the defaults are an unconfined shell: empty allowedDirectories means file tools read/write anywhere (proven against /etc/os-release), the shell is guarded only by a 32-command denylist, and telemetry is on by default.

tests.canonical_task: search 'Lantern Works GPU price comparison' and 'capital of Norway'
caveats: The failure shape is the defect: an agent reads an empty success as 'no matches exist', not 'search is blocked' — the silent-failure pattern Receipts exists to catch
The error text itself is honest (names bot detection, prescribes the remedy); serverInfo version is an empty string
tests.ground_truth: direct curl to DuckDuckGo's html and lite endpoints returned HTTP 202 bot-challenge pages in <1.2s — the egress is refused before any query is evaluated
tests.headline: Every search stalls ~31s, then returns zero results reported as success (isError: false). DuckDuckGo bot-blocks this egress, and the server's own prescribed [browser] remedy changed nothing. (Scoped: broken on bot-blocked egress.)

tests.canonical_task: create a table in a sandbox .duckdb file, insert planted rows, run a COUNT/SUM aggregate
caveats: Rung 1 and 2 failures are network-independent; rung 3's install failure is partly proxy-specific (prebuilt download failed, source build died extracting Node headers)
tests.ground_truth: hand-computed aggregates from the planted rows (never reached — no candidate started)
tests.headline: No DuckDB MCP candidate ever answered initialize: mcp-server-duckdb 1.1.0 crashes on today's SDK ('list_resources' removed), mcp-duckdb-server does not exist on PyPI, and duckdb-mcp's install collapsed after ~11 min on a legacy native binding.

tests.canonical_task: against a planted database: list tables, read a schema, run a SELECT aggregate (COUNT, SUM)
caveats: With two undocumented pins (mcp 1.17.0 + pydantic 2.11.7) the server itself is flawless: aggregates digit-for-digit, writes persist
Results are Python-repr text, not structuredContent; serverInfo claims version 0.1.0
tests.ground_truth: database planted with python3 sqlite3 (products: n=5, SUM price 110.49, SUM stock 540, plus a marker row); writes verified by reading the file directly with sqlite3
tests.headline: Reference server, dead on arrival: its unbounded mcp[cli]>=1.6.0 resolves SDK 2.3.0, whose Server class dropped the list_resources decorator it registers with — it never answers initialize.

tests.canonical_task: read a planted workbook: sheet names, specific cell values on two sheets, and one formula cell
caveats: Argument names changed from the older documented API (filepath -> path), though errors self-correct ('did you mean path?')
No filesystem boundary by default: any Excel file on the machine is openable unless launched with --allow-dir
tests.ground_truth: workbook planted with openpyxl (Units 10/20/30, formula =SUM(B2:B4) with NO cached result, marker EXCEL-MARKER-9021, value 42.5)
tests.headline: Best spreadsheet handling in the index: it evaluates formulas itself — returned the computed 60 where openpyxl had planted no cached value — with structuredContent throughout and an honest version handshake.

tests.canonical_task: convert planted documents (docx with heading/paragraph/table, simple PDF) to Markdown; bonus: convert example.com
caveats: The converter invents a spurious empty header row atop docx tables
Web conversion drops the page H1 — the same loss as test 001's readability path
serverInfo version is an empty string
tests.ground_truth: the planted heading, paragraph, table cells, and PDF markers; example.com's known page text
tests.headline: Both planted documents converted faithfully through a single URI-based tool (file:// and https://) — every planted string present and exact.

tests.canonical_task: extract text and metadata from a planted 2-page PDF with a unique marker on each page; search for the page-2 marker
caveats: mode='auto' downloads a HuggingFace embedding model before answering; the keyword mode one argument away is instant (2.3s)
Keeps a persistent SQLite extraction cache in the user's cache directory
tests.ground_truth: the planted markers, page count (2), and metadata fields
tests.headline: Extraction is exact — page count, metadata, both markers on the right pages, keyword search with correct bounding box — but the default search mode silently downloads an embedding model on first use and hung past 280s on this egress.

tests.canonical_task: in a planted vault (3 notes, a wikilink, a #tag, one subfolder note): list notes, search a planted unique word, read one note back
caveats: An empty hand-created .obsidian/ satisfies the gate (no running app or REST-API plugin needed), but that is nowhere documented
Error messages are exemplary; the server pressures clients toward a newer MCP protocol while working in legacy mode
tests.ground_truth: the planted note contents, byte-for-byte
tests.headline: Hidden gate: it refuses to start against a plain Markdown folder — the vault must contain an .obsidian directory, i.e. have been opened in the Obsidian app once — so any agent-created or git-cloned vault is rejected (VAULT_NOT_INITIALIZED). Once initialized, search hit exactly the right line and read-back was byte-exact with an etag.

tests.canonical_task: resolve the library 'react', then fetch documentation for the useState hook
caveats: Thin client for Context7's cloud: queries leave the machine, and a free-tier rate limit exists (not hit in 2 calls)
Resolve returns near-duplicate 'React' entries and its benchmark score does not rank the canonical one first; some chunks carry MDX tag residue
tests.ground_truth: react.dev's useState reference page, fetched directly in the same session
tests.headline: Genuine react.dev useState docs, verbatim-accurate against the live page, fully keyless — and its HTTP client honors proxy settings, making it the control case for this batch's proxy failures.

tests.canonical_task: get the DeepWiki index for modelcontextprotocol/servers, then read its overview page
caveats: Worst error manners in the index: a transport failure discards its cause; a rate-limit is relabeled nonexistence and delivered without isError
No API contract — it scrapes deepwiki.com HTML with happy-dom, so any redesign, bot wall, or rate limit silently becomes its behavior
tests.ground_truth: the repo's README fetched directly from GitHub, plus DeepWiki's page for the repo via an independent crawler (its claims verified 3/3, with file:line citations)
tests.headline: Two stacked failures, both misreported: its proxy-blind fetch dies as a bare 'fetch failed', and with the proxy honored an upstream HTTP 429 comes back as a successful 'Documentation not found' for a repo whose wiki demonstrably exists. (Scoped: proxy-egress/rate-limited environments; no successful call was observable from this VM.)

tests.canonical_task: fetch the transcript of 'Me at the zoo' (video jNQXAC9IVRw)
caveats: At least fails as a proper JSON-RPC error, unlike test 024's fake success
serverInfo reports 0.1.0 vs package 0.1.1; the lang parameter is required despite a documented default
tests.ground_truth: the video's documented transcript (Wikipedia's printed transcript, NPR, two other extractors' published outputs for this video ID): the elephants/'really long trunks' opening
tests.headline: 'Could not find captions' — false about the world: the captions exist, but YouTube serves this egress a watch page with zero caption tracks (verified by an independent scrape), and the server's own fetch is proxy-blind underneath. (Scoped: this environment.)

tests.canonical_task: search Airbnb for Austin, TX (a November weekend, 2 guests), then get details for the first listing
caveats: Its robots.txt politeness layer fails open — when the robots fetch fails it logs 'assuming all paths allowed' while the startup banner still claims robotsRespected: true

Best error manners of the batch's failures (isError, attempted URL, timestamps, structured logs); the design assumes Airbnb's pages stay scrapable from the user's IP, and both halves of that assumption failed in one test
tests.ground_truth: attempted independently: the server's own constructed search URL fetched via an independent crawler returned Airbnb HTTP 403 — no listing data was obtainable from this network by any route
tests.headline: The one server with no workaround at all: node-fetch v3 has no proxy support and the server offers no proxy option, so every request dies in 0.1s on TLS — and behind that wall, Airbnb itself 403s this infrastructure. (Scoped: proxy-egress networks.)

tests.canonical_task: generate a bar chart from planted data (quarters Q1-Q4 = 10/25/17/32)
caveats: The server sets no request timeout and upstream latency is bimodal: first call produced no response in 240s, a retry took 2.34s — clients with a 60s tool timeout will see un-diagnosable hangs
serverInfo version is the literal placeholder string '0.8.x' vs package 0.9.10; the CDN serves PNG bytes labeled image/jpeg
tests.ground_truth: the planted dataset, checked against the response's spec echo, a direct call to the rendering service with the identical spec, and visual inspection of the returned PNG (1800x1200, labels and proportions correct)
tests.headline: The chart is exactly right — but the 'local' server POSTs your data to Ant Group's hosted GPT-Vis service (antv-studio.alipay.com) and hosts the image on Alipay's public CDN at unauthenticated URLs.

tests.canonical_task: historical daily price for AAPL (2024-01-02) and basic quote/company info for AAPL
caveats: The live failure sits in yfinance's cookie/crumb session flow on proxy egress, not in Yahoo's API
A docstring promises start/end parameters that do not exist in the tool schema
tests.ground_truth: AAPL 2024-01-02 close 185.64 (EODHD and StockAnalysis agreeing to the cent; the assigned Stooq source was unreachable from this sandbox all evening). Yahoo's chart API itself answered 200 in 0.9s via curl from the same sandbox
tests.headline: Crashes at import as installed today (the mcp.server.fastmcp path was removed in mcp 2.3.0, which its unbounded requirement resolves to). Pinned to mcp 1.30 it starts — but both canonical calls timed out at ~60s and returned error strings with isError: false.

tests.canonical_task: geocode 'Statue of Liberty' and reverse-geocode the resulting coordinates
caveats: With a clearly labeled 6-line trust_env shim (proxy handling only), the data was perfect: geocode identical to direct Nominatim to 7 decimals (40.6892532, -74.0445482), reverse field-for-field identical
Requires Python >=3.13, which the README never mentions (the sandbox shipped 3.12)
tests.ground_truth: the Nominatim API queried directly in the same session
tests.headline: SDK-drift crash as installed; pinned, it still cannot reach Nominatim on proxy-egress networks — every call builds an aiohttp session without trust_env=True, so proxy settings are silently ignored and TLS dies on the intercept.

tests.canonical_task: current weather for New York City (the test-009 sequel: does a second weather server present next-hour data as current?)
caveats: The package summary is the unedited project-template placeholder 'Add your description here'; the whole README is one line naming no upstream API, so the assigned current-vs-next-hour check is moot
It also declares Requires-Python >=3.13, so it will not even 'install' on Python 3.12. A handshake census could never catch this; only install-and-look does
tests.ground_truth: not applicable — no server output exists to grade; the evidence is the published package artifact itself (wheel listing, pip show -f, run attempts)
tests.headline: The published wheel is empty: 1,139 bytes containing five metadata files and zero code — no module, no entry point, nothing that can answer an initialize on any machine — while pip install exits 0.

tests.canonical_task: in local mode (QDRANT_LOCAL_PATH, no server, no key): store planted texts with payloads, retrieve them back, check persistence across a restart (assigned as a vector-level task; translated 1:1 to this server's text interface — it exposes no raw-vector API)
caveats: It is a semantic text memory layer (qdrant-store/qdrant-find) — there is no collection/vector management API at all
First run eagerly downloads an ~87MB embedding model before answering initialize (12.8s unobstructed; in this sandbox it blew the 60s window until TMPDIR was redirected off the full /tmp)
Starts silently with no configuration at all
tests.ground_truth: the planted texts and payloads (exact-text query = embedding-space exact match; payload {label: quantum, slot: 2} verified intact)
tests.headline: Local mode works exactly as documented: exact retrieval, correct semantic ranking, persistence across a fresh process restart verified against the on-disk store — and it is the one package this wave whose own dependency pins (fastmcp 2.7.0, pydantic<2.12) kept it installable today.

tests.canonical_task: fetch the Hacker News frontpage feed (hnrss.org/frontpage); top titles/links must match the feed XML fetched independently
caveats: Rescuing it took three undocumented pins (fastmcp 2.7.0, mcp<2, pydantic 2.11.7), starting from test 009's exact McpError import crash
Second detector bug: pattern-matched URLs are verified by HEAD only — news.ycombinator.com/rss answers HEAD with 405 and was rejected too (GET returns the feed instantly)

The parser underneath is flawless: on the BBC feed (the one URL shape the detector accepts) the top 10 titles/links matched ground truth exactly, in order. All three failures are network-independent — it fails the same on its author's network
tests.ground_truth: hnrss.org/frontpage XML (20 items), news.ycombinator.com/rss, and feeds.bbci.co.uk/news/rss.xml, all fetched directly in the same minutes
tests.headline: Fails its canonical task: 'No RSS/Atom feeds found' for the live HN frontpage feed, because its detector judges a URL by spelling (end-anchored regexes) and HEAD response, never by content — the URL is never even fetched, and it burned 45.8s probing 18 guessed paths that all 404.

tests.canonical_task: look up the artist Radiohead (search, then lookup by MBID)
caveats: The misleading error is the defect: on any proxy-mediated network it sends the user debugging a healthy upstream
Cold npx initialize 13.4s; output is the raw API JSON firehose, unsummarized; a stderr banner discloses the project is AI-maintained
Ladder note: the two PyPI names and @modelcontextprotocol/server-musicbrainz are all 404 — this npm package is the only installable MusicBrainz server under the canonical names
tests.ground_truth: the MusicBrainz API fetched independently in the same session (Radiohead, id a74b1b7f-71a5-4011-9441-d0b5e4122711, type Group, score 100)
tests.headline: Search and lookup match the live API exactly — once the environment is proxy-aware. Under the standard sandbox env every call fails with 'MusicBrainz unreachable. The service may be down' while the API is verifiably up: Node's fetch ignores proxy variables and the server has no proxy configuration (NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY=1 fixes it instantly).

tests.canonical_task: get book details for ISBN 9780547928227 (The Hobbit, Mariner Books edition)
caveats: Scope: servers may exist under other names or as GitHub-only projects; the ladder graded the four canonical package names, which is where a user's search starts
The gap is purely the missing server — this is a listing-vs-reality finding, not a data finding
tests.ground_truth: openlibrary.org/isbn/9780547928227.json fetched independently (title 'The Hobbit', Mariner Books, 2012, 300 pages) — obtained and kept for the eventual retest; never used, because no server ran
tests.headline: No installable Open Library MCP server exists under any canonical name on either registry: all four ladder rungs return 404 / 'No matching distribution found', while the Open Library API itself is healthy and keyless.

tests.canonical_task: SpaceX company info and/or the latest launch, graded against api.spacexdata.com live
caveats: The r-spacex API is a single point of failure for every SpaceX tool built on it
Retest protocol: check upstream health first, or the test grades the API, not the server
tests.ground_truth: api.spacexdata.com/v4/company and /v4/launches/latest — unreachable all session: Cloudflare 522/525 on 8+ attempts over ~25 minutes
tests.headline: No installable SpaceX MCP server exists under any canonical name (all four rungs 404) — and the upstream community API was itself down the entire session, so no server could have served live data anyway.

tests.canonical_task: define the word 'serendipity'
caveats: The PyPI rung needs the exact two-pin resuscitation from test 009 (mcp==1.12.0 + pydantic==2.11.7); pinning mcp alone moves the crash into pydantic internals
Supplementary grading: once resuscitated, BOTH servers returned the ground-truth first definition word-for-word — packaging rot, not data rot
Version misreports on both rungs (npm serverInfo '1.0.0' vs package 1.0.6; PyPI serverInfo reports the SDK's 1.12.0 vs package 0.1.0); the PyPI server's tools are German-named
tests.ground_truth: api.dictionaryapi.dev/api/v2/entries/en/serendipity fetched independently (first definition quoted verbatim in the write-up)
tests.headline: Broken via every documented route: the PyPI server (dictionary-mcp-server 0.1.0) crashes at import on SDK drift, and the npm server (dictionary-mcp 1.0.6) ships no bin entry, so npx cannot run it at all. The other two ladder names are 404.

tests.canonical_task: search_repositories for "modelcontextprotocol"
tests.ground_truth: GitHub's public search API queried unauthenticated (total_count 1356, first item id 862570523 — exact match)
tests.headline: Canonical public search completes with NO token at all — the key-required premise is false for it, and the README never says so.
caveats: Completion was unauthenticated: for public search the token is optional, undisclosed in the docs
As-installed error shape is opaque (-32603 "fetch failed")
Decoy-token run hung >90s (no server-side timeout)
serverInfo reports 0.6.2 vs package 2025.4.8; npm marks the package deprecated (development moved to github/github-mcp-server)
tests.tester: batch-3 wave testers; reviewed by Pax

tests.canonical_task: slack_list_channels (limit 5)
tests.ground_truth: Slack's invalid_auth response via the token-as-parameter form (in ~0.85s)
tests.headline: Deferred — needs key. Best no-key gate in the batch (exits naming both required vars); the decoy-phase tool error is success-shaped.
caveats: Decoy-phase tool error is {"error":"fetch failed"} with no isError flag — a silent-failure shape
Canonical task not gradable without a real Slack token
tests.tester: batch-3 wave testers; reviewed by Pax

tests.canonical_task: API-post-search with query "test"
tests.ground_truth: Notion API unauthenticated 401 (partial; credentialed ground truth not obtainable from this egress)
tests.headline: Deferred — needs key. Worst failure shape in the batch: hangs in every configuration — no gate, no error, no answer in 90s.
caveats: No startup gate and no self-timeout: no-key, decoy, and decoy+proxy runs all hang silently
Docs claim 22 tools; 24 are listed
tests.tester: batch-3 wave testers; reviewed by Pax

tests.canonical_task: search for files matching "test"
tests.ground_truth: Not obtainable live (googleapis stalls from this egress even unauthenticated); graded on documented Google OAuth behaviour
tests.headline: Deferred — needs OAuth. The documented headless auth path is a silent dead end; fabricated saved credentials are accepted with zero validation.
caveats: Documented `auth` run headless prints "Launching auth flow…" then nothing — no URL, no error, hangs
Fabricated .gdrive-server-credentials.json accepted as "Credentials loaded." with no validation; search then hangs >90s
No-creds startup is clean (exit 1 with instructions)
tests.tester: batch-3 wave testers; reviewed by Pax
